Results.ReviewText:
Grill seems to be fairly well manufactured. It cooks nicely. The reasons for 2 stars are: 
*The propane tank regulator leaks propane out of it. We contacted Weber, but this unit is on back order so we were forced to buy an aftermarket one just so we could use our grill.
*The propane tank level indicator is kind of pointless. It has 2 red lines that both show most of the time. With a full, brand new 20lb tank, one line shows the tank is full and the other shows it is 1/4 full. 
*The left hand 'fold down' table end is also the one that you need to tilt the grill with to move it around. This quick fold table end is flimsy and should just be bolted on, folding it down is pointless. 
Other than that it is a decent grill, Hopefully it lasts a long time.
Results.Title: Decent grill, but could use improvement.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: I owned the previous Spirit 3 burner gas grill for over 10 years, and decided to upgrade to the latest model.  So far, so good!  It is lighter in weight, and like having the gas tank on the side of the grill.  HOWEVER, A WORD OF ADVICE - in the previous model, the burners ran sideways (OR LEFT TO RIGHT).  In the updated model, they run FRONT TO BACK.  Keep this in mind when you grill with INDIRECT HEAT - place the food over the middle burner that is turned off, FRONT TO BACK so that you don't burn some of your grilled food.

Results.ReviewText: I have owned four Weber grills over the years (one charcoal, one natural gas, and two propane).  I have found all to be consistently durable.  My recent purchase of the E-310 replaced a Genesis grill.  The E-310 heats quickly and provides uniform heat across the surface of the grill.  The grills are cast iron, and although they don't appear as thick as my old grill, they provide a consistent and even grill marking on the food.    The lid on the E-310 is not as heavy as my previous Genesis, but it seems to hold the heat allowing for an even grilling temperature, thus even cooking.  One side table folds down, which may be beneficial to someone desiring a smaller footprint for storage or use. The mounted temperature gauge is useful, but a point and read thermometer to check the temperature of the grills for searing temperature may be helpful.     After much research and comparison, the E-310 is living up to the excellent reviews and ratings it has garnered.
Results.Title: Quick to temperature, even cooking

Results.ReviewText: This has been the best grill I have owned, with my last one being a $400+ Kenmore.  I decided to assemble myself instead of some sketchy big box store associate scratching all my parts together.  This is definitely a quality build with very solid coated screws holding things together.  It should last a long time if kept covered and put away for the winter storage.  It heats extremely well and super even.  There seems to be no cold spots where one burger or part of a steak would not cook as well like it did on my other grills.  Also, several business carry this brand locally so finding replacement parts that aren't warrantied like the flavor bars will be easy to find.  I went with the non-cabinet version to save a few bucks but I actually like the big wheel barrow style wheels instead of the little casters.  I think it is easier to roll around.  My only complaint is that one of the side shelves folds down and they put it on the side opposite the wheels which makes it feel a little flimsier when moving like a wheel barrow.  No issues with it structurally but it would have been better designed on the other side but I suppose the propane tank would be in the way.
Results.Title: Cooks evenly!
